gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Soundcore's own US store sells the C50i at $39.98 today (list $69.99) while the AeroClip 2 sits at full price, $169.99. None states what the clip-ons in between cost: the 1st-gen AeroClip at $129.99, the C40i at $49.99, Shokz OpenDots Air at $129.95 and the OpenDots 2 at $199.95, which has replaced the sold-out OpenDots One. None of those cheaper models has the AeroClip 2's 2 VPUs (bone-conduction voice sensors), so you can't get its call hardware for less.
standout_why: I compared against HearWiki's AeroClip vs C50i page, which lists the 1st-gen AeroClip at $100 and the C50i at $70 and never mentions the AeroClip 2. SoundGuys' C50i page has $39.99 at Amazon and an MSRP of $69.99. On Soundcore's AeroClip vs AeroClip 2 blog the only models are those two, with no prices. ChatGPT's own answers already give $169.99 vs about $40, and one calls $69.99 the C50i's 'official price'. So the price gap itself is known. What's new is that the maker's own store already charges $39.98, plus current prices for the in-between rivals. The B&H compare pages returned 403, so I couldn't read them.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. At Soundcore's own store the gap is $130.01 (169.99 / 39.98 = 4.25×). The C40i ($49.99) and the 1st-gen AeroClip ($129.99) sit between them, but neither has the AeroClip 2's 2 VPUs or its Guinness G-MOS result. The OpenDots 2 costs $30 more and has 3 mics. So pay $169.99 only for calls; for anything else the C50i at $39.98 is the buy. Our page's Shokz row is out of date: the OpenDots One is still sold out, and its successor, the OpenDots 2, is in stock at $199.95.
